chapter: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
title: Richmond, Virginia, Johnson's Happy Pals and meeting Tyree Glenn
summary: Richmond work was poor at $3.50 a night; he and Milt Robinson heard Tyree Glenn practicing with Johnson's Happy Pals, then wired Helvey for a job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So that was the greatest thing that ever happened, you know, I think. And so now we go on and we finish these theater dates, then these guys tell us about going into Virginia, Richmond, Virginia. So we get into Richmond, Virginia, well, they seem to be pretty popular around there, but the way I gathered it, it wasn't the greatest band in town. I thought that the other band was much better. It was called Johnson's Happy Pals. Did you ever hear of them?
They played the Savoy, back, long years ago.

Yeah, Johnson't Happy Pals. And I got to know, through Tyree. [Glenn] See, we heard a guy practicing upstairs. Me and Milton Robinson was walking around one day, and we heard a guy practicing, so we went up there in the hall, you know, and it was Tyree, you know.
Yeah, but he was down there with the Happy Pals when I first met him.
Yeah, with Johnson's Happy Pals. I guess
he left Texas by that time, you know. Oh, he did.

Yeah, it was about 1930 or '31. So anyhow, we get down there and nothing happened. Every now and then we'd go out, everybody'd go out and get $3.50, and go out and make $3.50, so it wasn't nothing happening you know, to keep us really going. So then I sent a telegram to Helvey and asked him if he had an opening for trumpet and trombone. So he says we'll send you a ticket tomorrow, you know, and we got a ticket and went and joined Helvey.
